name: Man and the Dent de Man
subtitle: Man is a city in western Côte d'Ivoire, capital of the Montagnes district and known as the city of 18 mountains because of the ranges around it.

facts.label: Role
facts.value: Man is the regional capital of the Montagnes district, which includes the regions of Tonkpi, Guémon and Cavally

facts.label: Name
facts.value: Called the city of 18 mountains for the many ranges around it, which give it a mild, cool climate

facts.label: Dent de Man
facts.value: Twin rocks about 900 m high, symbol of the city, accessible to the top (press figure, not a surveyed altitude)

facts.label: People
facts.value: The indigenous population are the Yacouba (Dan), joined by Mahouka, Senufo and Baoulé from other regions

facts.label: Tourism office
facts.value: The regional tourism directorate of Man, created in 1973, worked until the crisis of 2002, when activities stopped

facts.label: Hotels
facts.value: At the time of the article (undated), of 47 hotels in Man only 32 were operating, with 262 rooms instead of 860

facts.label: Liana bridges
facts.value: A circuit of liana bridges runs from Man to Danané

parts.text: Man is a city in western Côte d'Ivoire, capital of the Montagnes district and known as the city of 18 mountains because of the ranges around it. Its symbol is the Dent de Man, a group of twin rocks. Local tourism sites declined after the 2002 crisis.

gaps: The description is summarised from the sources listed here and should be read against them.
